snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors Reveal Most Difficult Scenes To Film
snippet.description:
The adventures in the world of Harry Potter were nothing short of magical and chaotic! Throughout all the films, the Harry Potter actors faced their worst fears, performed intense stunts bravely, and got through some VERY long filming days. 
Filming the first movie was tough because of just how young all the kids were. Throw live animals into the mix who weren’t always on their best behavior, and you’ve got a recipe for disaster. The young ones were often tough to work with simply because they couldn’t keep focused for long enough, often giggling throughout takes - once it got so bad that the actor speaking had to do so from across the room to try and keep the kids cool! Spoiler alert: They couldn’t stop the giggling. The only thing more chaotic than the children's actors were the animal actors who made set life a nuisance for everyone.
Then there were the emotionally tough scenes to film - from Emma Watson being tortured by Helena Bonham Carter to Harry losing one of the most important people in his life. Emma Watson, Rupert Grint, and Daniel Radcliffe all had to overcome some very awkward feelings that came up about the kisses they had to film with each other. 
The stunts made for some exciting and painful days. Daniel Radcliffe was close to drowning, meanwhile, Robert Pattinson was seriously hurting after performing a stunt! No matter the feat, these actors overcame it to make sure the magic made it to our screen!

snippet.title: 15 Dangerous Scenes Johnny Depp Had To Film
snippet.description:
Whenever Johnny Depp signs up for a film, there’s a strong chance he’s signing up to find himself in very tricky and sometimes downright dangerous situations. The actor doesn’t always do his own stunts, but when he does, they still carry some pretty serious risk. 
Depp has done his fair share of car stunts - which included being hit by one over and over again! That said - it was as intimidating as working with a horse co-star, who, in a stunt gone wrong, wound up doing some serious damage to the actor’s body. 
Pirates of the Caribbean was a string of films involving risky situations - sword fighting anyone? Besides that, there were environmental dangers and perhaps most surprisingly of all, a safety strap that did WAY more damage than good. It wasn’t just Pirates when the environment was a concern though. One film saw Depp interacting with water so contaminated, he needed to be on a bunch of antibiotics before filming could begin! 
The struggles with filming scenes involving a lot of water didn’t end there though. Filming for the Fantastic Beasts franchise saw Depp getting pelted pretty hard with a waterfall of water on set - but he took it like a champ. 
Even way back in the early days of his career, Depp was pushing boundaries and testing his limits - and he went a bit too far with it when one of his costumes caused him to pass out in the middle of filming! Never underestimate the powerful heat-inducing combination of sun and leather. Despite all the odds, Depp came out of these films pretty unscathed!

snippet.title: Doctor Strange 2 Almost Had a Completely Different Ending
snippet.description:
When you crack open the multiverse, truly anything can happen. With the multiverses causing so much chaos, the possibilities of what could happen were endless - so the plot of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness changed QUITE a bit. We got a whole lot of characters that we didn’t expect - especially different versions of characters we know joining from other multiverses - but we didn’t get all those that had been planned initially. Rachel McAdams only plays two versions of Christine Palmer - any guesses how many more were planned? 
Since the production was delayed for various reasons - the pandemic of course, as well as director Scott Derrickson stepping down because of creative differences - and then, the whole MCU Phase 4 got shifted. The Multiverse of Madness film was meant to come before Spider: No Way Home, but re-arranging these two meant some major plot changes, especially because of all the chaos Doctor Strange began in Spidey’s movie. 
There was a script - but it wasn’t actually finished before filming began. In fact, it was about halfway through the filming process that anyone heard of how the movie might end - but even still - it continued to change! They did film quite a bit - including days and days of more re-shoots than normal. With all that footage, it’s not too surprising that Sam Raimi’s first cut of the movie came in at two hours and forty minutes. That being said - fingers crossed there will be plenty of deleted footage and extended scenes shared in the end - especially the alternate ending that caught us all off guard. This film changed multiple times, but with each chaotic change, they came one step closer to bringing this epic movie to the screen.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was total chaos behind the scenes. Any problem that could possibly have been thrown at them, was. From the director, Scott Derrickson quitting, to the entire script being scrapped, to Covid causing delays which caused subsequent delays, which meant overlap with other Marvel projects like WandaVision and Spider-Man filming, which meant the script had to be changed every time one of these projects contradicted what was already written, which led to six weeks worth of reshoots meant none of the actors knew what was going on, especially Rachel McAdams who was promised she’d get to play three Doctor Palmers and only got to play two. But that’s better than no Doctor Palmers like was promised in the first draft of Doctor Strange 2. Benedict Cumberbatch got to play many versions of himself meaning he got many moments of playing opposite himself which meant he was really just playing all by himself. Elizabeth Olsen got to try some new stunts and was surprised Marvel had it in them to still be innovative when it comes to flying. She also got to play opposite herself and was playing all by herself, but that wasn’t the only time she was alone. She never actually met John Krasinski or Patrick Stewart. Essentially, filming was a logistical nightmare, and yet, the cast still found it to be an enjoyable experience thanks to Sam Raimi’s charming personality and strong vision. On his way to becoming a globally-recognized star, Depp established iconic roles through wickedly painful transformations - like the terrifying Edward Scissorhands. snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors Who Had Crushes On Set
snippet.description:
Does anyone have some love potion? Whether or not magic was involved, there was plenty of romance and secret crushing on the Harry Potter set. When a bunch of young people spend hours on end with each other, playing pretend and experiencing hormones at the same time - well it’s bound to get a bit spicy!

Emma Watson was a crush for many of the actors on set - including some who were almost sibling-like to her! The actress had her fair share of crushes as well. The filmmaking tech had to evolve with Stark Tech. And these advancements to the Iron Man suit advanced Ultron and Ultron’s army as well. Imagine Marvel’s struggle if they started with Ultron and not Iron Man. It literally would have been impossible (or at least super expensive and bulky or incredibly paired down). Robert Downey Junior also had a genius idea that was implemented. The Hulk also got a few updates which are what led to Smart Hulk even being able to exist. snippet.title: 15 Embarrassing Scenes Elizabeth Olsen Had To Film As Scarlet Witch

Elizabeth Olsen is always looking fierce as the Scarlet Witch, AKA Wanda Maximoff. That is at least the impression we get seeing her on the big screen in the Marvel movies, but behind the scenes, she isn’t always so calm, cool, and collected. In some of her most intense scenes, the actress made some awkward stumbles, causing more injury to herself than anyone else! One of Olsen’s worst mess-ups on set wound up being enjoyed by the crew and cast on repeat - they even watched the stumble in slow motion! 
Olsen has an incredible relationship on and off-screen with her co-star Paul Bettany, but one unfortunate on-set incident led to their very first argument EVER - it even has a name: Snotgate. Bettany was responsible for making her laugh in the middle of multiple scenes. While the two actors are very close - Olsen has been far more used to Bettany as Vision, so when she saw him in the flesh there were some seriously weird vibes. Another co-star Olsen grew close with was her on-screen brother, Aaron Taylor-Johnson. These two could have a lot of fun on set - resulting in multiple messed-up takes. 
The Scarlet Witch has a very different experience when it comes to doing stunts. Her hand gestures and choreo are impressive on-screen, but her co-stars have made fun of her plenty of times because of just how wild she looks while doing the actions. One actor even referred to her as “being at a rave.” The actress has even shocked herself with her wildly bendy back.  
No matter how many times she fumbled or flubbed, Elizabeth Olsen always managed to bring the fire and power that made her the Scarlet Witch.

snippet.title: 15 Improvised Thor Scenes
snippet.description:
With people like Chris Hemsworth, Taika Waititi, and the rest of the Marvel crew in a room, you know it’s going to be a fun time on set - one that results in a LOAD of improv. Thor: Ragnarok was majorly influenced by improv, changing the script they started with immensely, but the changes they made really did work and made Ragnarok one of the best Marvel films there is. Jeff Goldblum let his freak flag fly as the Grandmaster, rambling on as long as the camera and director would let him. Which hilarious scene was completely improvised by the actor? There were a few of them - and one very special one didn’t even make the cut. 
Loki’s signature knife flip is, well, legendary, but who knew it was born from an improv moment? The first time it was captured on film, it didn’t get included - but luckily it’s made its way onto the screen plenty of times now - including in the Disney plus show named after the God of Mischief! 
Korg is a great character, but it was a bit surprising that he was so present on screen in Thor: Ragnarok. The character wasn’t slated for so much screen time, but anytime Taika Wititi got to go from behind the camera to in front of it, he kept the camera and banter going. It was thanks to keeping the work going that we got a very special speech from the one and only Thor. Who knew a one-line scene could turn into a very extended, but hilarious moment?!
Throughout the years, Chris Hemsworth and the Thor team have brought some of the most iconic lines and hilarious moments to life thanks to leaning into the improv so hard. Which improvised line or scene is your favorite? Let us know in the comments!

snippet.title: The Making Of The Bad Guys
snippet.description:
Behind The Scenes Of Dreamworks' The Bad Guys Animated Movie

The Bad Guys is rolling into theatres, bringing along with it a fresh new take on animation. It’s combining some 2D and 3D elements. It is making itself out to be an introduction to the genre of action for a younger generation, and also a cheeky nod to some of cinema’s best action movies like the Tarantino ones for example. The choreography and the action sequences were all working off of the same principle and that’s storytelling comes first. But also, now that we’re in the world of animation, how can we take this story type and subvert expectations? The music in this movie, like the animation style, is a blend of a bunch of different stuff. And Good Tonight almost wasn’t included in the movie! This is Pierre Perifel’s directing debut, not including a short film he’s done in the past. He hasn’t had enough time to be corrupted by the status quo. We’ve all got at least one unique story in us. Recruiting the actors was a pretty smooth endeavour. Awkwafina and Alex Borstein were more than happy to play strong characters. Craig Robinson was denied the opportunity to work improv skills but he did get to play around within his vocal range a lot and try a bunch of stuff so he still enjoyed his experience. Sam Rockwell and Marc Maron got special recording privileges that the rest of the cast didn’t necessarily get as much of. Lilly Singh and Zazie Beetz were just thrilled to be able to express themselves more freely than film usually allows. The Bad Guys is gonna be a good one, we can just tell.

snippet.title: 15 Disney Actors Painful Prosthetics And Costumes
snippet.description:
Disney is a world full of magic and action - but the costumes that come along with it aren’t always the most comfortable. From constricting costumes, heavy makeup, complex wigs, to heels higher than any heel should be - these Disney live-action actors have dealt with it all.
Cruella brought fashion as we’ve never seen before in a Disney film and as the saying goes, ‘Beauty is pain.’ Emma Stone dealt with heavy costumes and a very intricate mask. Emma Thompson struggled as well, dealing with high heels, champagne, and a bunch of dalmatians - yikes! When Maleficent was brought to the screen, Angelina Jolie went through a major transformation that involved painful prosthetics and custom-made leather horns. It might be many girls' dream to wear Cinderella’s glass slipper - but the reality isn’t so sweet. How did Lily James cope with a shoe that was so incredibly painful and ill-fitting? Richard Madden struggled with the size of certain costume pieces as well - his pants in particular. Diving into a whole new wardrobe for Aladdin and Jasmine saw beautiful results, but heavy and often overwhelming costumes for both Mena Massoud and Naomi Scott. Which actor didn’t wear a costume at all, but a giant motion capture suit that was made even harder to maneuver with ten-inch stilts involved?! This costume was so rough it actually affected the actor’s co-star as well, making their work together a bit tougher than they could have imagined.
These actors have smiled and worked through some VERY uncomfortable situations, but in the end, these films have looked pretty incredible. Those performers didn’t struggle for nothing!
